decisions.reason: Piqué upholstery fabric sits squarely within the firm's established weaving and upholstery know-how, and its dedicated webpage shows management can interpret its market response and keep refining it.

The semi-transparent bouclé decorative fabric draws on existing yarn-effect and decorative weaving skills, but it has only a brief website mention, which gives weaker early feedback to learn from, so the firm keeps it while it gathers evidence.

Flame-retardant jacquard curtain fabric builds on the firm's jacquard competence and its knowledge of contract-market FR certification, and its prominent presentation signals a strategic product the firm can improve through its own development work.

Double-face wool-blend decoration fabric is related to the firm's core weaving knowledge but gets only a minor mention, so its value is less clear, yet the evidence is too early to justify dropping it.

Wool bouclé leno weaving is the most technically distant variant and has limited visibility, which raises the risk of a drop, but it shares the bouclé knowledge base with Product B, so keeping it allows the firm to learn across both fabrics.
